transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Martinez (CTO - MetroClinic), Ravi Patel (Head of AI - MetroClinic), Maya Chen (Infra Eng - MetroClinic)

Auto-generated Summary (optional):
- Demo of Redwood Model Catalog and how to select open models for clinical summarization + triage.
- Benchmarks reviewed (p95 latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens) and compatibility matrix across A100/H100 and quantization profiles.
- Discussed VPC/on-prem options, SOC2/KMS, and pilot next steps.

Topics: Model selection, Benchmarks, Compatibility matrix, Private vs Hosted deployment, Security/compliance, Next steps/POC

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, joining with Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Dr. Elena Martinez: Good, thanks, excited to see the catalog. Quick context — we want to evaluate open models for clinical note summarization and triage, low latency for clinician workflows is huge.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Great. Priya will walk through the model catalog, compatibility matrix, and benchmarks, then we can talk infra and security.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Hi all — zooming into the Redwood Console -> Model Catalog. You can filter by use case, license, size, and verified performance. For MetroClinic, I'd filter for summarization and instruction-tuned models first.
[00:38] Ravi Patel: When you say "verified performance" — what does that mean? Are those Redwood-run benchmarks?
[00:42] Priya Nair: Yeah, we run an internal benchmark harness across sequence lengths and batch sizes. We report p50/p95 latencies, throughput (tokens/sec), and a cost estimate per 1M tokens for hosted and an estimation for Dedicated. Those are run on a standard hardware profile — usually A100 40GB and H100 for newer entries.
[00:58] Dr. Elena Martinez: We mostly run inference on-prem on A100s, but evaluating Dedicated and Private options. We need a compatibility matrix so we know which quantization profiles will work on our stack.
[01:07] Priya Nair: Totally. In the catalog each model has a compatibility entry — for example, model X1 supports q8_0 and q4_0 via our runtime, it's been tested with Triton and ONNX paths. For H100 we also publish kernel optimizations; for A100 there are slightly different memory/kv cache tradeoffs.
[01:24] Maya Chen: Quick question — our infra uses Kubernetes with Triton sidecars and strict egress controls. How invasive is Redwood Private?
[01:30] Jordan Lee: Redwood Private can fit both as a VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed nodes or as an on-prem package. For your K8s/Triton setup we usually run a thin agent and a private control plane — the catalog can show compatible build artifacts. We'll share the compatibility matrix for K8s + Triton.
[01:44] Priya Nair: Also note the runtime supports multiple kernel backends; sometimes the fastest path uses a fused kernel we ship for FP16 or q8_0 on H100, but on A100 memory layout and KV caching matters more so we recommend different batch sizes.
[01:58] Ravi Patel: Can you show an example benchmark? Latency numbers matter a lot — clinicians can't wait several seconds per note.
[02:04] Priya Nair: Sure, here's a typical row from the benchmark table — model Llama-X-13B-instruct (open license): p50 ~120ms per 32-token chunk on H100, p95 ~430ms, throughput ~3k tokens/sec with batch size 8; cost estimate for hosted configured at n1 is around $0.30 per 1M tokens (this is illustrative). On A100 with q8_0 those numbers shift — p50 ~160ms, p95 ~600ms.
[02:29] Dr. Elena Martinez: Those p95s are a bit high for interactive clinician use. Do you have lower-latency variants?
[02:33] Priya Nair: Yes — we recommend model families optimized for latency (smaller instruction-tuned models or distilled variants). There's also Redwood Optimize suggestions — if you enable aggressive prefix caching and smaller batch size per route you can get p95 under 300ms for many workloads. The catalog flags models with verified low-latency profiles.
[02:49] Ravi Patel: How reliable are the cost numbers for Dedicated? We have fixed budget so estimation matters.
[02:54] Jordan Lee: For Dedicated we provide committed capacity pricing. The catalog will show an estimated tokens/hour performance per GPU type; Dedicated pricing is a combination of reserved GPU cost + a per-token service fee. We'll send you a sample pricing spreadsheet that maps your throughput needs to committed GPUs.
[03:08] Maya Chen: On security — SOC 2, SSO, KMS, audit logs — can you walk through what is available?
[03:14] Jordan Lee: Sure. Hosted has SOC 2, SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning, and customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest if needed. Dedicated has VPC isolation and optional customer-managed control plane. Private deployments get the most flexibility including HSM/KMS integrations and local audit logs with configurable retention. We'll include the SOC 2 report in the security pack we send.
[03:31] Ravi Patel: Any gotchas on PHI? We need strict controls for protected health information retention and cannot have data leaving our VPC for certain flows.
[03:38] Priya Nair: For PHI we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with strict routing policies; our routing can pin traffic to customer-only models and disable any telemetry. We also support on-prem for fully air-gapped needs.
[03:48] Dr. Elena Martinez: Back to model selection: can you surface quality regressions over time? We need to ensure model updates don't break clinical outputs.
[03:55] Priya Nair: Redwood has versioning and rollout controls in Console — you can pin model versions, create canary routes, and set auto-fallback to a previous model if quality degrades. We also tie quality monitoring to prompt sets/evals so you can get regression alerts.
[04:08] Jordan Lee: Quick demo — switching to the catalog filter. I'm filtering for "clinical summarization" and license type "permissive". You can see rows with model name, size, license, p50/p95 latencies, throughput, and a short note on compatibility.
[04:24] [screen share noise / minor crosstalk]
[04:40] Priya Nair: Example compatibility matrix snippet: column headers include GPU family (A100/H100), quantization profiles (fp16, q8_0, q4_0), runtime path (native, triton, onnx), and notes (kv cache supported, fused kernels available). The matrix is automatically generated from our test runs.
[04:58] Ravi Patel: If we wanted to run a POC, would you recommend Hosted or Dedicated first?
[05:03] Priya Nair: For quick turnaround, Hosted is fastest to prototype; Dedicated is best if you want predictable throughput and data isolation. For MetroClinic I'd suggest a short Hosted benchmark or a small Dedicated trial depending on your compliance needs.
[05:16] Dr. Elena Martinez: Our security team will probably insist on Dedicated or Private for PHI. But a Hosted smoke test to validate quality would be fine as long as we don't send PHI.
[05:25] Jordan Lee: Agreed. For the POC we'll create a sanitized dataset and run a baseline on Hosted, then move to Dedicated trial on your A100s or our Dedicated pool for a head-to-head comparison.
[05:35] Maya Chen: On networking: can we do VPC peering + private endpoints, or do you require NAT egress?
[05:39] Priya Nair: We support VPC peering and private endpoints. For Private deployments you can avoid public egress entirely. We'll share a networking diagram in the security pack.
[05:48] Ravi Patel: About the compatibility matrix — are those tests synthetic or real-world (our clinical prompts)?
[05:52] Priya Nair: The matrix uses synthetic workloads to measure perf characteristics; we also run customer prompt sets during POCs to measure real-world latency and quality. That's why we encourage a short POC.
[06:03] Dr. Elena Martinez: Can you explain the fallback policy you mentioned earlier? If a model is overloaded or degraded, what happens?
[06:07] Jordan Lee: You can define routing policies by latency, cost, and region. If primary model is slow or returns errors, Redwood can fallback to a lighter model or a different region automatically. Rollouts can also be configured to send X% to canary.
[06:19] Ravi Patel: Any mention of tokenization differences between models? That affects both cost and latency.
[06:23] Priya Nair: Yes — the catalog also exposes tokenizer type and avg tokens per char for our benchmark inputs, so you can estimate token usage for your prompt sets.
[06:31] [short silence as Priya pulls up a chart]
[07:00] Priya Nair: One more datapoint — when a model supports KV cache and prefix caching, for conversational workloads we see cost reductions of 30–50% depending on prompt reuse. Redwood Optimize has suggestions to enable that automatically.
[07:18] Dr. Elena Martinez: Good — our triage flow will reuse patient context a lot so caching is important.
[07:22] Ravi Patel: What about quantization impacts on hallucinations? Any observed quality drop for q4_0 or q8_0?
[07:29] Priya Nair: There is always a tradeoff. Our evaluations flag models where quantization causes measurable quality regressions on your eval sets. For clinical use we often recommend testing q8_0 first and validate against your prompts; some models handle q4_0 well, others don't. We'll include model-specific notes in the spreadsheet.
[07:44] Jordan Lee: I'll also note that for mission-critical workflows we recommend canarying and human-in-the-loop verification for a period post-rollout.
[07:52] Maya Chen: Latency targets — can you guarantee p95 under 300ms for certain models?
[07:56] Priya Nair: For smaller models and optimized runtime profiles yes, but for larger 13B+ models it's harder. If your target is 300ms p95 we can map the requirement to model family + hardware + batching config and propose a Dedicated configuration that meets it.
[08:10] Ravi Patel: Are there any licensing pitfalls with open models we should watch out for?
[08:14] Priya Nair: The catalog shows license type — permissive vs restricted. We advise legal to review model licenses before production. We can filter out models with incompatible licenses.
[08:23] Dr. Elena Martinez: Ok, let's talk timeline. We have a compliance review the week of June 29. If we want a POC before then, what's feasible?
[08:31] Jordan Lee: We can stand up a Hosted benchmark within 48-72 hours with a sanitized dataset. A Dedicated trial provisioning may take 1–2 weeks depending on capacity and contract terms.
[08:41] Maya Chen: For the Dedicated trial, what's the minimum commit?
[08:44] Jordan Lee: We have small reserved pools for trials — typically 1-2 GPUs for a short-term trial; contract terms are flexible for pilot customers. We'll propose a trial commit in the follow-up.
[08:53] [minor audio glitch]
[09:05] Priya Nair: Demoing the compatibility matrix export — you can export CSV or JSON of the matrix; we'll include a pre-filtered CSV for MetroClinic.
[09:15] Ravi Patel: Great. On POC success criteria we'll want: (1) p95 latency under X ms for summarized workflow, (2) token cost per summary below Y, (3) no PHI egress for private flows, and (4) quality thresholds on a held-out clinical eval set.
[09:29] Jordan Lee: That's helpful — we'll capture those as POC success criteria and align the trial.
[09:35] Dr. Elena Martinez: Any more demo slides?
[09:38] Priya Nair: Quick look at model detail page — shows eval snippets, typical prompts, tokenizer, compatibility, and benchmark curves (latency vs sequence length). Also notes on recommended quantization and batching.
[09:51] Ravi Patel: About the optimization tooling — can Redwood Optimize automatically propose batching changes?
[09:55] Priya Nair: Yes — it analyzes your request distribution and suggests batching/caching/quantization profiles. It can also propose model family swaps for cost vs quality.
[10:05] Dr. Elena Martinez: Ok let's recap the next steps and owners.
[10:10] Jordan Lee: Recap: Jordan to send benchmark spreadsheet + pricing and model catalog export; Priya to send compatibility matrix and quantization recommendations; Maya to share networking constraints and timeline for compliance review. We'll schedule POC scoping for week of 2026-06-22.
[10:25] Ravi Patel: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood?
[10:29] Jordan Lee: None on our side; just need your sanitized dataset and confirmation on PHI handling.
[10:34] Dr. Elena Martinez: We'll prepare a sanitized set and legal will review licensing.
[10:38] Jordan Lee: Ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack.
[10:42] [meeting ends]
